BraiinsPoolParams.description: Tunables for a simulated Braiins Pool account.

hashrate_ths.description: 5-minute-average hashrate the account hovers around, in TH/s.

payout_amount_btc.description: Amount of every completed payout, in BTC.

payout_period_s.description:
Seconds between payouts, landing on the unix-epoch grid (86400 =
daily at midnight UTC). `null` = an account that has never paid out:
no history, no estimate, null progress.

status.description: HTTP status every endpoint returns; 401/403 = the denied account.

workers_active.description: Worker counts by state, as `/user/workers/current` reports them.

Celsius.description: A temperature in degrees Celsius, above absolute zero

Formula1Params.description: Tunables for a simulated Nexus Formula 1 deployment.

careers_status.description:
Status of the careers-derived resources (the statistics table,
the driver index, the per-driver cards) — the trio the real deployment
503s while a fresh instance warms up.

careers_warmup_secs.description:
Seconds those resources 503 for before reaching `careers_status`.

A fresh deployment derives them on first boot and answers nothing
until it has — the widget's first sight of the API, and the state
it is least likely to handle.

image_dir.description:
Images the payloads point at, in a directory relative to the blueprint.
Laid out as the widget's own artwork is: `headshots/<NN>.gif`
`logos/<NN>.png` and `flags/<country>.png`, beside `circuit.png`.
Omitted, nothing is served and every image URL 404s onto the widget's placeholders.

season_underway.description: `false` scripts the off-season: no next race, empty standings.

session.description: The running session; `idle` scripts a quiet week.

sprint.description:
Whether the weekend runs a sprint, which replaces two practices
with a sprint and a qualifying of its own.

stale_secs.description:
Added to every envelope's `cache_age_secs`;
larger than the resource's `ttl_secs` scripts stale-while-revalidate.

start_lap.description:
The lap the session is already on when the simulator starts.

Gaps, tyre ages, pit stops and retirements accumulate over a race,
so a session opened at its first lap shows a widget almost nothing.

A scenario names the lap whose state it exists to show. Note that a
race board seats only its leading rows, so whatever sorts to the tail
— a retirement, an exclusion, a car a lap down — is visible on the
full-field board alone.
